stimulus.body: L'extrait ci-dessous sert à vérifier la compréhension de cette forme. «-e.» Parmi les quatre réponses, une seule s'appuie sur le texte lui-même.

questions.stem: La consigne de cet item est «Identify pronounced ending / Check singular. / The one ending of a regular -er verb that is pronounced». Quelle réponse en découle ?

options.misconception: mistakes a surface feature of "None" for the governing rule

questions.explanation: What settles the item is the relation stated in the passage: only -e is pronounced in regular -er verbs. On that basis "-e" is the supported choice. Option D ("-ons") fails because it picks silent plural; Option B ("-ent") fails because it picks silent plural; Option C ("None") fails because it mistakes a surface feature of "None" for the governing rule.

questions.topic: Where the French r is made in the mouth

stimulus.body: Dans une note de travail consacrée à ce point, on lit: «Think single place.» Quatre affirmations sont proposées; une seule est conforme à ce que la note établit réellement.

questions.stem: Avec «Locate r / Think single place. / Where the French r is made in the mouth» en téte, quelle option est conforme au texte ?
questions.explanation: Close reading of the note yields this rule: the French r uses one articulation place. On that basis "Where the French r is made in the mouth" is the supported choice.

questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.topic: oi as a single sound, as in bois

stimulus.body: L'extrait ci-dessous sert à vérifier la compréhension de cette forme. «One sound.» Parmi les quatre réponses, une seule s'appuie sur le texte lui-même.

questions.stem: Avec l’indice «Recognise oi / Treat as digraph. / oi as a single sound, as in bois», quelle option est réellement appuyée par le texte ?

options.misconception: Splits the digraph into two sounds
Overcounts the sounds in the word
treats "No sound" as if it followed from the evidence

questions.explanation: The passage gives the controlling distinction: the digraph oi in bois represents a single vowel sound, so Option A wrongly splits the pair into two sounds, C overcounts the sounds in the word, and D denies that the combination makes any sound at all. On that basis "One sound" is the supported choice. Option A ("Two sounds") fails because it splits the digraph into two sounds; Option C ("Three sounds") fails because it overcounts the sounds in the word; Option D ("No sound") fails because it treats "No sound" as if it followed from the evidence.

questions.topic: The written s between vowels

stimulus.body: L'extrait ci-dessous sert à vérifier la compréhension de cette forme. «s or z by word.» Parmi les quatre réponses, une seule s'appuie sur le texte lui-même.

questions.stem: Avec l’indice «Handle s between vowels / Check the word. / The written s between vowels», quelle option est réellement appuyée par le texte ?

options.misconception: treats "Always silent" as if it followed from the evidence
substitutes a familiar but inapplicable case for the relation the passage establishes

questions.explanation: Close reading of the note yields this rule: the written s between vowels is s or z by word. On that basis "s or z by word" is the supported choice. Option B ("Always silent") fails because it treats "Always silent" as if it followed from the evidence; Option C ("Always z") fails because it substitutes a familiar but inapplicable case for the written s between vowels; Option A ("Becomes nasal") fails because it mutates consonant.
